newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay airport put through anti-hijack drill.
newsitem.headline: Bombay airport put through anti-hijack drill.

text.p: Indian security authorities caused a brief scare when they staged an anti-hijack drill at Bombay's domestic airport on Sunday, airport and airline officials said.
A Boeing-737 flight from Bombay to Mangalore with 17 passengers and six crew aboard was used for the dummy run.
"Yes, there was a mock exercise involving flight CD 179A from Bombay to Mangalore," Mukesh Bhatia, Alliance Air's chief manager at Bombay's Santa Cruz airport, told Reuters.
He said the flight had been due to take off at 12.30 p.m. local (0700 GMT), but was held on the tarmac.
At 1.30 p.m. the bogus hijacker informed the control tower that he wanted $100,000, Bhatia said. The hijacker also demanded to speak to Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral.
Two hours later the security forces had regained control of the plane and the control tower was informed that the passengers had been released.
Airport authorities and control tower officials confirmed that the exercise had been a drill.
